method: Check reported reader obstacles against current source and reached official pages. No product edits.

evidence: src/content/docs/tools/dr-memory.md:64 labels https://drmemory.org/page_install.html as Windows installation guide and asks for release/architecture verification.
The linked page is a platform selector. Its Windows destination explains MSI/ZIP/PATH setup but does not answer the requested compatibility check.
checks.scope: Instructional handoff issue; no claim that Dr. Memory is incompatible with Windows or the target.

evidence: src/content/docs/tools/address-sanitizer.md requires clang, linker/libraries, matching runtime and architecture but supplies no environment preflight.
The linked LLVM guide is a compiler/runtime reference; the rendered Windows command is already labeled illustrative.
checks.scope: A concrete supported Windows setup would make the exercise easier. Missing installed tools is an environment boundary, not a failed product command.

evidence: Dr. Memory uses a placeholder executable. The memory guide already links the ASan bounds example with a correction.
checks.scope: Merge with the complete Windows first-run path; do not duplicate every tool tutorial.

evidence: src/content/docs/guides/api-testing.md:17 requires Python 3.12 but line 72 uses the unqualified python interpreter.
src/content/docs/tools/schemathesis.md:60 identifies Python 3.11+ for 4.33.1. The fresh recorded run succeeded on Python 3.13.15.
checks.scope: Clarify tested runtime versus supported prerequisites and select/check the interpreter. No claim that all compatible versions were tested.

evidence: The API guide supplies fixture commands and an external CLI reference but no own-API command.
examples/http-api/run_schemathesis.py exposes port/output and fixes the schema URL to loopback /openapi.json with selected positive server-error checks.
checks.scope: The fixture works. Add a small adaptation example while preserving its deliberately narrow scope; no requirement to turn the demo wrapper into a general scanner.

evidence: src/content/docs/tools/pylint.md:59 gives prose instructions; install and run links are in the sources list.
The agent successfully used those official links and installed Pylint 4.1.3.
checks.scope: Recoverable external-documentation handoff, not a broken tool or unavailable installer. A direct inline next action and link to the shared combined recipe can address much of the friction.

evidence: The Python guide names a checkout and working directory but has no clone/download or cd command.
Both successful execution scenarios used the already available checkout after discovering the site link. Fresh file acquisition was not exercised.
checks.scope: Confirmed instruction omission, untested impact. Add a short shared get-the-example step if retaining the basic-reader audience; do not claim that GitHub downloads failed.

evidence: src/content/docs/guides/python-checks.md:79 supplies adaptation prose but no command targeting a reader-selected directory.
examples/python-checks/run_checks.py:74 only accepts bad/good; the fixture deliberately selects Ruff F401.
checks.scope: The documented demo succeeds. Make the next real-project invocation explicit without implying the two-check fixture supplies a complete project configuration.

excluded_as_product_defects: Browser automation visibility and clipboard-read limitations.
Unavailable locally installed analyzers or compilers by themselves.

grouped_recommendations.title: Add concrete own-project and own-API next steps
grouped_recommendations.change: Add a short command example to each existing guide, naming working directory, target path or schema/test URL, configuration, report location, and selected scope. Link deeper options instead of copying full references.
grouped_recommendations.acceptance: Starting after the successful demo, a reader can identify exactly what to replace and run a bounded check on a second synthetic project/API without designing the command from a reference manual.

grouped_recommendations.title: Complete one Windows memory-checking first-run path
grouped_recommendations.change: Choose one supported host/toolchain/target combination; link exact setup and compatibility evidence, add a short readiness check, and carry one existing faulty/corrected example through the tool.
grouped_recommendations.acceptance: A fresh reader can verify prerequisites, run the known failure and correction, locate the report, and explain its limits. If setup is unavailable, the next action and support boundary are explicit.

grouped_recommendations.title: Clarify and verify the API interpreter requirement
grouped_recommendations.change: Distinguish supported versions from the recorded environment, and show how to check/select the intended Python before creating the venv.
grouped_recommendations.acceptance: The prose and command select the same intended runtime; a reader with a different default Python can tell whether to proceed or install/select another interpreter.

grouped_recommendations.title: Make Pylint first steps easier to reach
grouped_recommendations.change: Put direct setup/run links and a minimal invocation near Start with a small package; point combined lint/type readers to the maintained shared recipe.
grouped_recommendations.acceptance: The reader can reach an installation command, file-check invocation, and output explanation from the start section without locating multiple source citations.

grouped_recommendations.title: Explain how to obtain and enter the example directory
grouped_recommendations.change: Add one shared get-the-example instruction with a clone or download route and explicit working-directory command, linked from recipes.
grouped_recommendations.acceptance: Test acquisition from the published site in a directory without an existing checkout; keep this opportunity provisional until that test.

positive_results: Home task shortcuts and catalog summaries enabled relevant tool selection.
The Ruff/mypy faulty and corrected runs matched the documented findings and statuses.
The API service supplied a useful target, reset/correction steps and retained reports; the compatible-runtime recovery reproduced the selected scanner outcomes.
The ASan example explained error type, access/allocation location, correction and exercised-path limits clearly.
